title: King's Handwritten 'I Have a Dream' Draft Goes on Display for the First Time
summary:
The only known draft of one of the most famous speeches in American history is on display for the first time. It is the Reverend Martin Luther King Jr.'s handwritten draft of the speech he gave at the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom in 1963. The seven-page document is on show at the National Center for Civil and Human Rights in Atlanta, through Sunday.

It is written in cursive, in blue ink on yellow legal paper. King scratched through sections and reworked them, changing a word here and a phrase there. 'You see him on the page wrestling with the words,' said Jill Savitt, the center's CEO.

King first titled the speech 'Normalcy Never Again.' Here is the surprise: the draft does not include the speech's most famous lines, 'I Have a Dream.' King improvised those words that day, August 28, 1963, before a crowd of 250,000 people on the National Mall.

The draft was found by Xernona Clayton, an Atlanta civil rights leader. Now 96, Clayton said she found the papers tucked in a manila envelope while cleaning out her late husband's old desk in the late 1990s. Her husband, Edward Clayton, was one of King's speechwriters. She rediscovered them a couple of years ago and decided it was time to share them with the world.

The manuscript will be offered for auction through Christie's in New York in January, where the auction house says bids could top $10 million. Before that, it will also be on display in Chicago. Former Atlanta Mayor Shirley Franklin visited the center last week and pointed to a photograph of the crowd at the march. She said she was sitting by the reflecting pool. 'What we remember is the part that came from his heart,' she said.
why_it_matters: The draft shows how one of history's most famous speeches was shaped word by word, and it reminds us that its best-known lines were spoken from the heart in the moment.

keywords.explanation: Cursive is a style of handwriting in which the letters in a word are joined together.
If someone improvised words, they made them up on the spot instead of reading them from a written text.
A manuscript is a handwritten or typed document, such as an early draft of a speech or book.
An auction is a sale in which people offer increasing amounts of money until the highest offer wins the item.
A manila envelope is a large envelope made of thick, light-brown paper.

Rare handwritten papers can be put on display in a museum and later sold at auction, where buyers offer money to own them.
